question: Which of the following Harappan structures had a thin lining of bitumen to prevent the seepage of water ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Great Bath**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Great Bath is one of the most prominent architectural structures found in the Harappan civilization, located in Mohenjo-Daro (present-day Pakistan).
 
• The structure was designed as a large water tank made of baked bricks and featured a thin lining of bitumen to make it waterproof and prevent water seepage.
 
• The Great Bath is believed to have been used for ritualistic or religious purposes, as water held a significant cultural and spiritual value in ancient Harappan society.
 
• It measures approximately 12 meters in length, 7 meters in width, and 2.4 meters in depth, with steps leading into the tank on both ends.
 
• This structure highlights the advanced engineering and urban planning skills of the Harappan people, especially in water management and drainage systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bitumen in Harappan Structures:**

 
 
• Bitumen, also known as natural asphalt, was used as a waterproofing agent in Harappan architecture.
 
• It was applied as a thin layer to prevent water from seeping into the walls or floors of structures like the Great Bath.
 
 
 
• **Urban Planning of Harappa:**
 
 
• The Harappans were known for their well-planned cities, which included wide roads, drainage systems, and standardized brick sizes.
 
• Public structures like granaries, baths, and assembly halls were an integral part of their urban design.
 
 
 
• **Ritual Significance of Water:**
 
 
• Water played an essential role in the religious and cultural practices of the Harappan civilization.
 
• The Great Bath may have been a site for communal or ceremonial purification rituals involving water.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Harappan Structures:**
 
 
• Granaries were used for storing surplus grains and were located near agricultural areas or riverbanks.
 
• The drainage systems were highly advanced, with covered channels to carry away wastewater from residential areas.
 
 
 
• **Discovery and Excavation:**
 
 
• Mohenjo-Daro was discovered in 1922 by archaeologist R. D. Banerji.
 
• The excavation revealed significant insights into the social, economic, and cultural aspects of the Harappan civilization.
